nodes.name: Robust and efficient visual odometry using colored point cloud maps via dual-sparsity and hierarchical optimization
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable localization is fundamental to navigation in GNSS-challenged environments, yet monocular visual odometry (VO) inevitably suffers from drift without global constraints. Point cloud maps can provide global corrections to mitigate this drift. However, existing heterogeneous feature registration methods fail to fully exploit the shared information between vision and point clouds. This limitation results in suboptimal localization accuracy, reduced robustness, and increased computational overhead. To address these issues, we propose a visual odometry system based on colored point cloud maps, which leverages both the global point cloud map as a constraint and the shared modality (color) between the colored point cloud map and the camera to ensure localization accuracy and robustness. The system consists of two main components: sparse colored point cloud construction and visual localization. In the sparse colored point cloud construction module, we introduce a map sparsification strategy that associates visual gradients with point clouds, ensuring that the retained sparse point cloud preserves salient visual gradient information, thereby reducing computational costs. This strategy is further incorporated into the vision-to-map matching stage, forming a “dual-sparsity matching” scheme. In the localization stage, we propose a hierarchical optimization-based iterative Kalman filtering algorithm, which performs multi-level iterative optimization over multi-resolution images to prevent localization from getting trapped in local optima while enhancing accuracy. Experiments on public and self-collected sequences demonstrate significant gains in both accuracy and efficiency. Compared with a representative map-based method (DSL), the proposed approach reduces ATE (RMSE) by $$52\%$$ 52 % – $$95\%$$ 95 % across multiple challenging sequences, with a representative improvement from 1.883 to $$0.152\,\text {m}$$ 0.152 m on R3live_5 ( $$91.92\%$$ 91.92 % reduction). Against the learning-based I2D-Loc++, our method achieves accuracy gains of up to $$76.6\%$$ 76.6 % and maintains robust tracking in extreme cases (e.g., R3live_3/4 ) where I2D-Loc++ and ORB-SLAM3 fail due to visual degradation. Furthermore, the system maintains near real-time efficiency, reducing total processing time by up to $$47.7\%$$ 47.7 % (e.g., from 121.11 to $$63.34\,\text {s}$$ 63.34 s on Whu_1 ). Even under severe geometric degeneracy, our tracker remains robust with an ATE of $$0.076\,\text {m}$$ 0.076 m , whereas geometry-only LiDAR–IMU localization degrades to $$9.23\,\text {m}$$ 9.23 m .

nodes.name: Enhancing sparse multi-view super-resolution with unified multi-plane image spatial representation
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract The popularization of multi-camera systems and multi-view image capture has led to the emergence of sparse multi-view image super-resolution (MVSR) as a promising research direction. The primary approach to sparse multi-view super-resolution (SR) currently involves extending traditional single-view SR and stereo SR frameworks, i.e., extracting features from each view and performing pixel-domain alignment and fusion to leverage cross-view reference information. However, this straightforward framework has two main drawbacks. First, performing cross-view fusion in the pixel domain disregards the spatial perception information that multi-view images provide. Second, feature alignment and fusion across views introduce considerable redundant and repetitive computations, which hinders further scalability to more viewpoints. This paper proposes a novel sparse multi-view SR framework based on a unified spatial representation reference. Specifically, the proposed method first computes a multi-plane image spatial representation from the multi-view images. This multi-plane image (MPI) representation encapsulates all the information from each view and has spatial perception. Subsequently, an upsampled reference image is rendered from the MPI representation for the low-resolution views. A high-low frequency separation fusion network is then proposed to upscale the input low-resolution images based on the rendered reference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for recovering high-frequency details.

nodes.name: Polarimetric image restoration with adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization-based color correction
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Optical electronic devices often exhibit certain limitations when attempting to capture underwater images, such as poor contrast, color casts, and blurry details. To improve the image quality of underwater scenes, polarization-based methods are introduced to enhance the underwater image. Nevertheless, the enhancement performance of most current methods is limited by their manual backscatter region selection processes and their disregard for color and brightness restoration. In this paper, we propose an underwater polarimetric image restoration method based on adaptive backscatter light estimation and angle of polarization (AoP)-driven color correction. Specifically, we construct an adaptive standard deviation of Gaussian filter-based on the entropy of the input image to capture the complete backscatter light. Afterward, we correct the color casts based on a reference channel and two gain coefficients, fully considering the color attenuation introduced by the difference in the AoP, and simultaneously utilize the AoP map and the gray-world assumption to spatially modulate the correction process. Finally, we comprehensively consider the brightness information of HSV and normalized backscatter light estimation to design an adaptive gamma revision function, thus naturally adjusting the enhancement results. The enhancement results on the underwater polarimetric image dataset show that our method achieves a good enhancement ability with high contrast, reasonable appearance, and natural brightness. Moreover, the extensive histogram distribution and image segmentation experiments demonstrate that our enhancement results have almost the same histogram distribution for the r, g, and b channels and can yield more accurate segmentation effects.

nodes.name: An Intelligent Computer Vision Framework for Duplicate Part Detection in Complex CAD Assemblies
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract:
Duplicate components in large-scale Digital Mock-Up (DMU) assemblies present a significant challenge to product integrity within Digital Twin environments operating on integrated OEM Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms. These duplicates, often referred to as structural redundancies or doubloons, are characterized by geometrically identical or equivalent components occupying the same spatial location without corresponding justification in the Bill of Materials (BOM). Such inconsistencies arise from increasing assembly complexity, tool integration issues, and limitations of conventional scripting-based validation approaches.
Existing duplicate detection methods rely heavily on manual inspection and isolated tool functionalities, making them impractical for large-scale assemblies. While interference analysis tools can detect spatial conflicts, they cannot reliably distinguish between valid engineering overlaps and unintended duplicate conditions. Consequently, a more structured and automated validation strategy is required.
This paper presents an automated computer vision-based methodology developed within an OEM Digital Twin environment to address these challenges. The proposed framework combines interference-data extraction, image-based overlap assessment, automated duplicate screening, Active Feedback Learning, and BOM-integrated validation within a unified workflow. The methodology transforms interference-derived information into structured analytical features and uses Red Percentage–based overlap evaluation to identify potential duplicate conditions.
The proposed approach enables scalable duplicate detection across complex assemblies while reducing dependence on manual review. Validation on production-scale automotive DMU datasets demonstrated significant reductions in engineering effort and substantial filtering of non-actionable interference records. By integrating computer vision analytics, feedback-driven noise elimination, and product structure validation, the proposed framework improves Digital Twin data integrity and supports efficient engineering workflows in modern OEM PLM environments.

nodes.name: A Computational Intelligence Framework for Data-Driven Shape Optimization Using GRA and GA-BPNN
nodes.abstract: Abstract Traditional product shape optimization suffers from single-objective tuning, low prediction precision, and inefficient nonlinear mapping between design variables and performance. To address the limitations of conventional Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), such as weak optimization ability and low prediction accuracy in shape design, this paper proposes an intelligent optimization framework integrating Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) and Genetic Algorithm-optimized BPNN (GA-BPNN) for purple clay teapot shape design. First, a standardized teapot shape database is established, and morphological decomposition and factor analysis are performed to extract and screen key shape parameters. GRA is then applied to quantify correlations between parameters and objective dimensions, determining four core inputs for the neural network. On this basis, GA is used to optimize the initial weights and thresholds of BPNN, overcoming slow convergence and local optima issues. The GA-BPNN model achieves accurate nonlinear mapping from subjective design requirements to three-dimensional shape parameters and outputs the globally optimal shape combination. Experimental results and user tests show that the optimized scheme exhibits superior objective matching and user satisfaction, with significantly higher prediction accuracy and convergence efficiency than the standard BPNN. This work establishes a complete intelligent optimization workflow for product shape design, which supports high-precision multi-parameter optimization and nonlinear function mapping. The proposed hybrid method has strong scalability and can be extended to general shape optimization and multi-parameter decision-making tasks, providing a data-driven approach for intelligent design applications.

nodes.name: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): Selection of active galactic nuclei and star-formation emission with machine-learning techniques
nodes.venue: Astronomy & Astrophysics
nodes.abstract: Sources detected by recent large-area radio surveys require robust classification and characterisation. The Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) is a prime example of machine-learning (ML) techniques efficiently enriching existing catalogues with classifications and derived physical properties that would be impractical to obtain from spectroscopy or colour selection alone. We aim to build a labelled sample of sources in the EMU pilot survey (EMU-PS, at qty 944 , with rms ∼ over qty 30 270 in the southern sky) classified as being dominated by active galactic nuclei (AGNs) or non-AGN processes including star-formation. We will then use this sample to examine radio properties and redshift-dependent trends. We applied a pre-trained multi-stage ML pipeline to optical-to-infrared photometry of EMU-PS sources to derive classifications and photometric redshifts, which we used to compute additional radio properties, including luminosities. We increase the known number of AGNs and non-AGNs in the EMU-PS by more than a factor of ) up to z ∼ , and by nearly a factor of ) for z łesssim , respectively. In extrapolating these numbers for the full EMU survey, we expect to recover more than ) spectral indices. (recall 96 5 (recall 94 1 million AGN candidates. A non-negligible low-redshift subsample of selected non-AGNs shows radio luminosities in excess of those expected from star formation alone, revealing detachment between photometric and radio classification. Radio-derived properties show expected trends for luminosities and a lack of evolution for in-band (qtyrange range-units=single, range-phrase= -- 800 1088 The ML-based pipeline provides a scalable way to produce large catalogues for the ongoing EMU survey and future Square Kilometre Array observations and reveals that multi-wavelength analysis can uncover radio populations and trends often missed by colour cuts or spectroscopy alone.

nodes.name: YOLO vs. diffusion networks for underground pipe detection: a case study using ground penetrating radar data
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract The accurate detection and mapping of underground pipelines are critical for urban planning and infrastructure resilience. This process is critical to prevent catastrophic failures, minimize service disruptions, and maintain the structural integrity of public works projects. Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a prominent technology for the automated detection and precise localization of subsurface utilities. However, the current dependence on manual data interpretation is a major bottleneck, often resulting in high temporal and operational costs. Consequently, this research addresses these limitations by presenting a performance analysis of two distinct deep learning architectures–YOLO (You Only Look Once) and Diffusion-based neural networks–for automated underground pipe detection. Utilizing a specific dataset of GPR scans, the models were evaluated using a robust five-fold cross-validation framework to assess mean Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (mAP50) and inference latency. The experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-based architectures provide a superior balance between detection precision and real-time processing efficiency. While five-fold cross-validation established a mean mAP50 of approximately 80% for the YOLO models, the YOLOv12n architecture exhibited superior performance on the independent test set, achieving an mAP50 of 94%. In contrast, DiffusionDet models were characterized by lower precision and significantly higher latency. While this study focuses on a single-site case study, the findings establish a foundational baseline for the selection of deep learning architectures and provide a framework for future research into the adaptation of these models across varying geological conditions.

nodes.name: Topological Core and Spatial Configuration Differentiation of Qing Dynasty Educational Buildings: An Investigation of Hunan Academies and Confucian Temples
nodes.venue: Buildings
nodes.abstract: Academies (shuyuan) and Confucian temples (wenmiao) respectively embody the traditions of scholarly instruction and ritual observance in traditional China, representing two significant architectural typologies within the ancient Confucian cultural and educational systems. However, existing research largely consists of qualitative descriptions of individual types, lacking cross-typological quantitative comparisons based on unified metrics. Focusing on 26 extant Qing Dynasty academies and 15 Confucian temples in Hunan Province, this study employs spatial genotype theory to construct a quantitative framework integrating “functional configuration,” “plan morphology,” and “Justified Plan Graph (JPG) topology.” Spatial genotypes are identified through the matrix of “Functional Type of the Topological Core” versus “Configurational Type.” The results show the following: (1) The overall functional composition of the two building types is quite different, but the main institutional functions are not necessarily concentrated in the topological core, which is dominated by transitional spaces such as courtyards, corridors and entrance halls. (2) The degree of axial concentration and spatial depth is remarkably higher in Confucian temples, whereas the branching rate is significantly higher in academies. Notably, spatial depth is highly sensitive to the encoding of entrances. (3) The distribution of “spatial genotypes” between the two building types shows no statistically significant differences. In terms of topological core functions, both types are dominated by transitional spaces, while Confucian temples tend toward axial organization and academies toward branched connectivity in terms of configurational relationships. The study developed an analytical path of “topological core identification and functional attribute determination—configurational relationship analysis—two-dimensional spatial genotype extraction,” providing empirical reference for the classification and protection of academy and Confucian temple heritage and the quantitative study of the spatial generation patterns of traditional public buildings.

nodes.name: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models
nodes.abstract: Conceptual abstraction and gender are two equally central aspects of the human mind, yet they have traditionally been studied in isolation from one another, as though they were fundamentally separate. Here, we find gender and abstraction are systematically linked throughout the space of concepts spanning single (N = 40,000) and multi-word expressions (N = 67,000): across billions of words and millions of images on the internet — and across numerous measurement techniques, including human and AI classifications — more abstract concepts are more associated with men, a pattern we show replicates in languages around the world. This male abstraction bias not only holds across semantic domains, but it also maps onto grammatical structure: verbs and adverbs are more abstract and more male-coded, revealing a system-wide trace of stereotypes accentuating agentic qualities in men. Furthermore, we show this bias readily emerges in the free associations humans and AIs produce in controlled online tasks, indicating its psychological internalization and its algorithmic reproduction. These findings identify a latent structure in conceptual space that unifies a range of stereotypes: for example, framings of women as more embodied, emotional, and warm, versus men as more cognitive, rational, and competent; as well as erroneous views of men as better at mathematics, science, and engineering. More broadly, by analyzing an unprecedently large, multimodal sample of online data, we provide culture-wide evidence of gender as a core organizing principle shaping conceptual space far beyond the characterization of people and social roles.

nodes.name: Spatial distribution and health risk assessment of airborne and soil-bound lead in an industrial zone
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract The emission of pollutants from human activities in industrial zones poses significant challenges to air quality and soil health, particularly in semi-arid environments. Utilizing 56 sampling stations and geostatistical modeling, this study conducted a comprehensive, multi-pathway assessment of lead (Pb) dynamics in the ambient air and surface soil of the Salafchegan Special Economic Zone (SSEZ) in Iran. The results revealed a marked disparity between atmospheric Pb levels (mean: 12.88 µg/m³) and concentrations in the soil (mean: 3.05 mg/kg). This discrepancy is attributed to the region’s high wind energy (DPt = 936), which causes the resuspension of deposited dust and limits Pb accumulation in surface soil, effectively retaining the metal in the atmospheric phase. Both Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) produced comparable prediction errors in cross-validation; however, OK was selected for final mapping because it provides a measure of prediction uncertainty (kriging variance) and accounts for spatial autocorrelation. The OK-based maps revealed significant heterogeneity (CV = 58.36%) and identified industrial hotspots. A probabilistic health risk assessment, conducted via Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations, indicated that the total non-carcinogenic risk remained below the permissible Hazard Index threshold (HI < 1); however, children consistently demonstrated greater vulnerability than adults to exposure to this pollutant. These results show that local climatic factors strongly influence the environmental fate of Pb, indicating the need for targeted air quality management and regular monitoring around industrial zones.

nodes.name: Satellite-derived vegetation indices and machine learning for food crop yield prediction: A systematic review of methods, performance and research gaps
nodes.venue: Plant Science Today
nodes.abstract: Crop yield prediction is essential for global food security, but the current methods for yield estimation are labour-intensive, time-consuming and have limited spatial and temporal coverage. This systematic review focuses on consolidating the evidence from the 32 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018–26 that are concerned with using both satellite-derived vegetation indices (VIs) and machine learning (ML) to predict food crop yields. A preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA)-based search resulted in the identification of studies on rice, wheat, maize, soybean, sugarcane, sorghum and barley across different geographic regions. The evidence clearly shows that across all food crops, Random Forest (RF) is the most consistent ML technique, with an R² of 0.70–0.96 based on crop and region and deep learning approaches like long short-term memory (LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) show higher temporal pattern recognition, but much greater numbers of labelled data are needed. Multi-index approaches consistently outperform single-index approaches, with those extracted from Sentinel-2 performing well in situations where normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) loses sensitivity due to canopy saturation at high biomass levels in dense-crop canopies. Sentinel-2 is the most frequently used satellite platform (over 65 % of the analysed studies) and Google Earth Engine (GEE) has become the most used data processing environment. There are still gaps in the standardisation of benchmarking metrics, the representation of smallholder and tropical farming systems, the integration of data across phenological stages and the cross-regional transferability of models. This review consolidates evidence and presents clear priorities to move precision agriculture yield forecasting toward global food security applications.

nodes.name: STAC-LIO: Robust LiDAR-Inertial Odometry in dynamic environments via spatiotemporal consistency perception and adaptive observation noise covariance
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Aiming at the challenge of balancing suppression of dynamic interference and the preservation of effective observation constraints in complex dynamic scenes for LiDAR-Inertial Odometry (LIO), a dynamic robust LIO framework based on spatiotemporal consistency perception and adaptive observation noise covariance (STAC-LIO) is proposed. In this framework, an active collaborative mechanism for mutual feedback enhancement between dynamic perception and state estimation is featured. It can adaptively adjust observation confidence, improving environmental adaptability of LIO in complex scenes. Within this framework, the proposed dynamic point detection algorithm based on temporal occupancy and core extended neighborhood refinement-compensation mechanisms (TOP-CEN) quantifies the dynamic-static attributes of point clouds. At the state estimation layer, the dynamic-static attributes provided by TOP-CEN are introduced into the adaptive robust iterative extended Kalman filter (AR-IEKF). They guide the adaptive inflation of observation noise covariance, thus suppressing dynamic interference while retaining effective observation constraints. The posterior pose output by AR-IEKF is further fed back to TOP-CEN, providing a more reliable spatiotemporal consistency benchmark for its dynamic-static attribute discrimination. This reduces dynamic point misjudgment caused by pose estimation errors. This mutual feedback enhancement mechanism combines perception-assisted localization and localization-enhanced perception. It helps improve the completeness of dynamic point detection and the stability of state estimation. We compared TOP-CEN and STAC-LIO with 7 dynamic point removal methods and 4 LIO algorithms, respectively, on 20 sequences from 5 datasets. Compared with state-of-the-art online methods, TOP-CEN achieves an average relative improvement of 8.09% in the F1 score on the SemanticKITTI dataset. For localization accuracy, STAC-LIO achieves maximum improvements of 42.47% and 12.20% on the KITTI and UrbanLoco datasets, respectively. We also conducted real-world experiments using a mobile robot platform. Overall, STAC-LIO improves localization accuracy and robustness in complex dynamic environments while constructing static maps.

nodes.name: Research Progress of Encoder–Decoder Network in Image Fusion
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Image fusion is a research hotspot in the field of computer vision, which obtains complementary information from the different modal images and then presents it in a comprehensive, highly information-cohesive fused image. Encoder–decoder networks are an important technical method in the field of image fusion. This paper reviewed the research status and development of the encoder–decoder networks in the field of image fusion from the following aspects: Firstly, the 21-image fusion-related datasets and the 27 open-source codes of deep learning-based image fusion are summarized. Secondly, the model structure of encoder–decoder networks and the basic principles for image fusion based on the encoder–decoder network are described. Thirdly, encoder–decoder networks fusion models are summarized into four aspects: convolutional auto-encoder network (CAE Net), sparse auto-encoder network (SAE Net), U-shape encoder–decoder network (U-net), and variational auto-encoder network (VAE Net). In U-net, there are five types: U-net incorporating residual connection mechanism (Res U-net), U-net incorporating dense connection mechanism (Dens U-net), U-net incorporating multiscale connection mechanism (MS U-net), U-net incorporating attention mechanism (Att U-net), and U-shaped encoder–decoder networks (U-net) combined with Generative Adversarial Network (GAN U-net). Fourthly, the existing image fusion evaluation metrics are summarized from both subjective and objective aspects. Fifthly, the application of encoder–decoder network in five kinds of image fusion, such as multi-exposure image fusion, multi-focus image fusion, infrared and visible image fusion, medical image fusion, and remote sensing image fusion, are summarized. Finally, there is a discussion of the main challenges faced by encoder–decoder networks in the image fusion domain and an outlook on future directions. This paper systematically analyzed the application of encoder–decoder networks in the image fusion areas, which has positive implications for the progress of image fusion technology.

nodes.name: Reliability-weighted neighbor consensus for fault-tolerant spectrum sensing in 6G smart factories
nodes.venue: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
nodes.abstract: Persistent probability inversion, rather than ordinary report noise, is the fault considered in this study. Ten simulated receivers map four I/Q features to local occupancy probabilities and communicate soft states for ten ratio-consensus rounds. Unlabeled median/MAD agreement accumulated over time supplies most of the weight; instantaneous confidence is restricted to a bounded correction. We test five SNRs, 0–30% faulty nodes, and five seeds with thresholds fixed on clean validation data. At 30% faults, AUC changes from 0.7619 to 0.7859 and false-alarm probability from 0.5295 to 0.4165, but detection probability falls from 0.8017 to 0.7881. The 20% case shows the same conflict: 0.8499 to 0.8567 AUC and 0.3400 to 0.2663 false-alarm probability accompany a detection change from 0.8207 to 0.7993. Historical weighting is therefore useful for persistent faults at this simulated operating point, not evidence of a deployed 6G-factory system.

nodes.name: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
Reference-Guided De Novo Retrieval of 3D Chromatin Organizational Features with Representation Learning
nodes.abstract: Chromosome conformation maps reveal spatial genome organization through recurring contact patterns, some associated with established architectural features and others with less understood biological processes. Identifying instances of a pattern across these maps is necessary to investigate its biological associations and recurrence across experimental settings. However, conventional feature callers typically target predefined patterns, offering limited support when researchers can provide examples of a feature of interest but lack a dedicated detection method. We introduce Chromatin Fetch (C-Fetch), a reference-guided retrieval framework that uses examples of a desired feature and a contrasting class to rank and assign contact-map patches at provided candidate coordinates. C-Fetch learns a reusable representation through weakly KL-regularized 3D autoencoding of structurally related, non-temporal Hi-C and Micro-C patches without architectural feature labels. We demonstrate retrieval of biologically defined contacts, visually specified patterns, and established architectural features. Polycomb-guided retrieval identifies contacts enriched for PRC2-associated signals, exceeding enrichment from loop-guided assignments at 5 kb, while queries resembling condensed domains retrieve patches with progressively stronger rectangular enrichment at higher ranks. Loop-guided retrieval increases aggregate focal enrichment relative to complete Mustache proposal sets across four held-out maps, and selected contacts show greater focality loss after cohesin depletion than matched remaining candidates. Retrieval also extends to Region Capture Micro-C and HiChIP, with ranking agreement retained across biological replicates and reduced sequencing depths. Together, these results establish reference examples as a flexible means of specifying contact-map features of interest, enabling biological investigation, exploration of visual patterns, and refinement of existing calls across datasets and technologies.

nodes.name: Neutralizing Misleading Visual Cues: An Attention-Driven Encoder–Decoder Framework with Auxiliary Forensic Reconstruction for Video Deepfake Detection
nodes.venue: AI
nodes.abstract: As deepfake generation methods are constantly evolving, there is a need for new methods that can detect subtle manipulation artefacts in video content, both in terms of spatial and temporal characteristics. In this study, an encoder–decoder architecture is proposed, where the classification and forensic reconstruction are performed simultaneously at the encoder and decoder side, respectively. The architecture consists of a six-layer convolutional encoder to obtain spatial representations from uniformly sampled facial frames of 128 × 128, and a two-layer bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) to model temporal dependency within the sequence of eight facial frames. An attention-pooling mechanism additionally highlights the most instructive temporal characteristics and yields a brief sequence-level representation for binary categorization. In parallel, a forensic decoder reconstructs 64 × 64 Laplacian residual maps, encouraging the network to learn edge-level and texture-level manipulation traces. The framework is trained end-to-end using a weighted combination of cross-entropy classification loss and L1 reconstruction loss. Experiments on the Celeb-DF dataset, comprising 1168 cropped face videos, achieved 93% training accuracy, 90% frame-level classification accuracy, and an ROC-AUC of 0.92. Complementary analysis across spatial, frequency, and temporal feature domains showed that spatial texture characteristics provided the clearest class separation, while the forensic reconstruction branch achieved an MSE of 0.010. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of jointly integrating spatial encoding, temporal sequence modelling, attention-based aggregation, and reconstruction-guided forensic learning for deepfake detection.

nodes.name: MIsCORE-RIUD: Paper VII: Residual Classification, Minimum Common Support, and the Observation Boundary
nodes.abstract: Gravitational-wave detection pipelines are highly successful at identifying modeled and coherent signals, but the evidential meaning of post-model structure is a different question. This paper does not dispute established LIGO detections, nor does it claim that LIGO formally labels every residual sample as noise. It asks a narrower methodological question that became unavoidable during MIsCORE-RIUD: when H1 and L1 do not express the same merger-local residual structure in an identical lower-order form, does failure of a stronger representation-level consistency criterion justify rejecting the remaining structure before its higher-order organization is tested? RIUD answered operationally by requiring minimum concurrent support rather than global detector identity. A local candidate could not be carried by one detector alone: h1_z=min(H1 family), l1_z=min(L1 family), and network_z=min(h1_z,l1_z). Only candidates surviving both detector support conditions could enter the frozen NODE set, and only connected multiscale NODE organization could be promoted to PATH. Paper VII retrospectively audits that rule rather than inventing a new one. Four frozen evidence layers are decisive. First, Paper II gives 13/13 detector-resolved map compatibility and a fixed-path raw-strain population statistic of 1.171221 with 0/100,000 empirical-null exceedances, while a stricter eventwise coherence contract yields 0/13 FDR05 survivors. Second, a 96-event, 57,696-row detector-representation audit is directionally non-equivalent: median out-of-fold gain is -0.2044 for H1->L1 and +0.6496645697 for L1->H1; the final 9,999 whole-event null gives 0/9,999 exceedances (plus-one p=0.0001). Third, the NODE-conditioned median log10(L1/H1) high-band balance reverses from +0.4373 at 10 ms to -0.7916 at 80 ms. Fourth, controlled relational replay is invariant to detector swap, constant gain, and constant phase rotation, but sensitive to relative timing and time-varying phase; lower-order NODE occupancy can change while the higher-order PATH persists. The resulting claim is bounded but consequential: failure of global representational identity is not, by itself, evidence that the residual structure is noise. Under the tested RIUD contracts, concurrent local support followed by higher-order structural survival is a defensible promotion rule. Paper VII therefore closes a specific methodological vulnerability in the earlier RIUD lineage: the cross-detector rule was not an ad hoc relaxation introduced to rescue a result, but a frozen minimum-support contract later tested against the observation system itself.

nodes.name: Lightweight Architecture Optimization for Car Logo Detection Based on Visual State Space Models
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Car logo detection is a challenging fine-grained perception task characterized by small object scales and high inter-class similarity. In such scenarios, discriminative cues mainly reside in subtle local textures rather than global structures. Although State Space Model (SSM)-based detectors, such as Mamba-YOLO with its ODMamba backbone, provide efficient long-range dependency modeling, they often struggle to maintain spatial alignment and semantic consistency during multi-scale feature fusion. This limitation reduces their effectiveness in fine-grained discrimination. To address these issues, this paper proposes LVSS-Net (Lightweight Visual State Space Network), a unified framework with three key components. First, Multi-Scale Semantic Alignment (MSAA) preserves spatial resolution while enhancing semantic consistency across feature pyramid levels through adaptive normalization and attention-based fusion. Second, Dynamic Content-Aware Reconstruction (DCR) introduces learnable content-adaptive offsets to model variable sampling positions during feature upsampling, mitigating scale-induced information loss and boundary blurring. Third, Global–Local Saliency Modulation (GLSM) combines parameter-free global saliency modeling with local texture enhancement via a lightweight LTE module to capture fine-grained discriminative patterns. Extensive experiments on the VLD-11 fine-grained car logo dataset and the TT100K traffic sign detection dataset demonstrate that LVSS-Net achieves 98.3% mAP@0.5 with only 1.5 M parameters. The proposed method reduces model complexity by 73.5% compared to the Mamba-YOLO baseline while maintaining competitive detection performance. These results demonstrate its effectiveness in resource-constrained fine-grained detection scenarios.

nodes.name: LGSTNet: Efficient Local–Global Collaboration for Heterogeneous Remote-Sensing Landslide Segmentation
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Purpose: Landslide segmentation from remote sensing imagery is challenged by scale variation, irregular morphology, blurred boundaries, and confusion with spectrally similar backgrounds. This study aims to develop an efficient framework that coordinates heterogeneous input regulation, local structural preservation, and hierarchical semantic modeling. Methods: LGSTNet is organized around two coupled design principles. An input-configuration-oriented local–global encoder combines input recalibration, a shallow Ghost branch, and a compact three-stage Swin Transformer. An accuracy–efficiency-oriented compressed context-fusion strategy enhances the deepest Transformer feature through compressed multi-scale, directional, and global context branches and integrates multi-level representations using a lightweight projection–fusion decoder. Results: Experiments were conducted on the Jiuzhai Valley, HR-GLDD, and Landslide4Sense datasets. On Landslide4Sense, LGSTNet achieved the best F1-score, foreground intersection over union (IoU), mean IoU (mIoU), and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) among the seven evaluated models, reaching 64.01%, 47.07%, 72.81%, and 63.39%, respectively, with 3.79 M parameters, 2.39 G FLOPs, and 63.93 frames per second. On HR-GLDD and Jiuzhai Valley, it provided competitive segmentation performance with favorable inference efficiency, although it did not outperform every baseline. A within-dataset input-configuration experiment on Landslide4Sense further showed that the F1-score of LGSTNet increased from 42.87% with RGB input to 64.01% with the full fourteen-channel input; SegFormer exhibited the same overall trend, increasing from 42.50% to 61.56%. Conclusion: LGSTNet provides a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off across the three evaluated remote-sensing configurations. The within-dataset input-configuration results provide additional evidence that the complete system can benefit from the information available in the full multi-channel input, while the cross-dataset comparison alone is not interpreted as causal evidence that channel number or modality richness by itself explains the observed performance differences.

nodes.name: Integrating Space Syntax and User Movement Observation to Identify Potential Human Activity Energy Harvesting Zones in Campus Buildings
nodes.venue: DIMENSI: Journal of Architecture and Built Environment
nodes.abstract: Energy consumption in campus buildings continues to increase with the intensity of building use and user activities, while research on human activity-based energy harvesting remains predominantly focused on energy conversion technologies, with limited attention to the relationship between spatial configuration and the distribution and concentration of user movement. To address this gap, this study integrated Space Syntax analysis and field observation to identify candidate circulation zones for future human activity-based energy harvesting applications.in the HC-A Building of Soegijapranata Catholic University Semarang. The spatial configuration analysis was carried out using DepthmapX through Visibility Graph Analysis (VGA), with Connectivity and Visual Integration analysed independently. Connectivity was used to determine preliminary candidate circulation areas based on the internal spatial configuration, while field observation was used to identify the distribution of actual user movement, particularly at main access points influenced by external movement sources. The Connectivity-based analysis identified 631 m² (67.85%) of the total analysed circulation area as preliminary candidate areas. Afterintegration with field observations, the final candidate area increased to 661 m² (71.08%), representing an additional30 m² or 3.23 percentage points primarily around the main access zones, with relatively high observed movement that was observed but was not fully captured by the preliminary Connectivity-based classification. The findings indicate that the distribution of actual user movement is associated not only with the internal spatial configuration but also with building access functions and their connections to external movement sources. Thus, integrating spatial configuration analysis with field observation provides a spatial basis for identifying candidate circulation zones for subsequent technical assessment of energy output, device performance, and installation feasibility of human activity-based energy harvesting applications.

Infrared–Visible Image Fusion for Enhanced Visual Carrier-Landing Perception
nodes.venue: Mathematics
nodes.abstract: Visual perception for autonomous carrier landing requires high stability and environmental adaptability. Under complex maritime conditions, such as nighttime, sea fog, and low visibility, visible images are easily affected by illumination changes and atmospheric scattering, resulting in reduced target contrast and weakened scene structures. Infrared images can provide relatively stable target information through thermal radiation differences between targets and backgrounds, but offer limited texture and fine-grained structural details. To address the difficulty of simultaneously preserving target saliency and scene structural integrity with a single modality, we propose CLSC-Fusion, an infrared–visible image fusion method for enhanced visual carrier-landing perception. Based on FusionGAN, CLSC-Fusion introduces an infrared gradient loss and a visible intensity loss to enhance the preservation of infrared salient information and visible details. An eight-neighborhood Laplacian operator with diagonal neighborhoods is further introduced into the gradient constraint to strengthen responses to multi-directional edges and texture variations. Meanwhile, the generator architecture is improved to enhance the representation of fusion features. Experiments on the TNO dataset show that CLSC-Fusion achieves competitive results in Spatial Frequency, Average Gradient, edge preservation, and PSNR, while maintaining high levels of Standard Deviation and SSIM. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the proposed improvements. Case studies in visual carrier-landing scenarios demonstrate that CLSC-Fusion effectively integrates infrared target responses with structural information from flight decks, islands, and sea–sky backgrounds, providing more complete visual information for carrier-based aircraft perception under complex environments.

nodes.name: Explainable vision Mamba–Kolmogorov–Arnold learning for multi-temporal monitoring of vegetation stress and land degradation in drylands
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract Monitoring vegetation stress and land degradation in dryland environments is challenging because short-term spectral variability can obscure persistent ecological change. Complex deep-learning architectures also do not necessarily provide higher predictive performance or independently validated explanations. The study developed and evaluated an explainable Vision Mamba (VMamba)–Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) framework for multi-temporal vegetation monitoring in Badr Al-Janub, Saudi Arabia, using Landsat observations from 2015 to 2025. Multi-temporal vegetation and moisture indices were integrated with terrain variables, while a geographic partition defined training, validation, and locked independent-test subsets. On the locked independent-test set, VMamba–KAN achieved an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 78.76%, frequency-weighted Intersection over Union (FWIoU) of 71.28%, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 20.06%, and Macro-F1 of 25.11%. The CNN baseline achieved higher OA, FWIoU, mIoU, and Macro-F1 values than VMamba–KAN. Cohen's Kappa was 0.424 for VMamba–KAN and 0.404 for the CNN baseline. The Kappa difference is reported separately and is not interpreted as evidence of overall or class-balanced predictive superiority. Temporal analysis identified broad improvement in vegetation condition toward 2023 followed by partial deterioration in 2025 rather than continuous landscape-scale degradation. Integrated Gradients provided descriptive attribution patterns associated with VMamba–KAN predictions. Full-scene softmax probabilities provided descriptive predictive-confidence information and were not interpreted as calibrated uncertainty estimates. The results emphasize temporal persistence, geographic evaluation, class imbalance, predictive performance, and cautious interpretation of attribution evidence.

nodes.name: Efficient Residual Learning With Multi-scale Attention for Robust Coal-rock Image Classification
nodes.abstract: Abstract Robust coal-rock image classification is challenging because visual differences among coal, gangue, limestone and sandstone are often subtle and can be obscured by lighting variation, dust, humidity, sensor noise and complex texture similarity in mining environments. This study proposes an efficient multi-scale attention residual learning framework for image classification, aiming to improve the balance among classification accuracy, parameter efficiency, convergence speed and cross-domain robustness. The proposed network introduces a residual convolutional block that integrates efficient multi-scale attention for spatial and channel-wise feature enhancement, while replacing conventional convolutions with depthwise over-parameterised convolution during training to improve convergence without increasing inference complexity. The model is evaluated on three public natural image benchmarks, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and CINIC-10, and on a proprietary four-class coal-rock dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks while maintaining a moderate parameter scale. On CIFAR-100, it improves classification accuracy over several attention-enhanced residual baselines, and on COALSet-4 it obtains a substantial improvement compared with the corresponding residual baseline, indicating stronger adaptability to fine-grained industrial visual patterns. Ablation experiments further suggest that both the multi-scale attention component and the modified convolutional operation contribute to accuracy gains and faster convergence. Visual inspection of attention regions indicates that the model can focus on discriminative local texture structures. The results demonstrate the potential of efficient multi-scale residual learning for coal-rock recognition and related industrial image classification tasks. Our source code is available at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20841285}{10.5281/zenodo.20841285.

nodes.name: Development and external multicenter validation of a multimodal nomogram integrating MRI findings and PSA biomarkers for individualized risk assessment of clinically significant prostate cancer
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
nodes.abstract: Background Accurate identification of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥2 [GG2+]) remains challenging because prostate-specific antigen (PSA) lacks specificity and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alone may lead to unnecessary biopsies. We developed an interpretable model combining routinely available MRI and PSA-related variables. Methods This retrospective multicentre study included a development cohort from Center 1 (n = 260) and external validation cohorts from Centers 2 (n = 91) and 3 (n = 29). Multivariable logistic regression integrated age, PI-RADS score, free-to-total PSA ratio, and PSA density (PSAD). Performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, reclassification, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. External validation used the fixed model without refitting. Results In the development cohort, 112 patients (43.1%) had GG2+ disease. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.872 (95% CI 0.823–0.914) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.864, outperforming PSAD alone (AUC 0.807; ΔAUC = 0.065, 95% CI 0.012–0.120; P = 0.013). Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer Lemeshow P = 0.797). The model improved reclassification (continuous NRI = 0.789; IDI = 0.206) and provided greater net benefit than the comparator strategies at the evaluated threshold probabilities of 20%–30%. At a 25% threshold, it avoided 17 biopsies per 100 patients without additional missed GG2+ cancers compared with PSAD ≥0.15 ng/mL/cm 3 . External AUCs were 0.832 (95% CI 0.733–0.917) and 0.880 (95% CI 0.690–1.000). Conclusion The MRI–PSA model showed favorable discrimination and satisfactory development-cohort calibration, with potential clinical utility for GG2+ prediction. Prospective validation in representative non-Chinese populations and diverse healthcare systems is required before broader clinical adoption.

nodes.name: Controlled PCA-Based Generation of Synthetic Object Images for Satellite SAR Data Augmentation
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Nowadays, synthetic aperture radars are widely used on various satellite imaging platforms. The high availability of SAR imagery makes it very popular in various automatic object detection systems. However, the visual interpretation of SAR data is difficult even for experts, which poses the primary challenge in preparing the data required for training and evaluating deep learning models. Therefore, using data augmentation techniques to expand the original training dataset is a popular approach. In this paper, a method of synthetic SAR object image generation is proposed using Principal Component Analysis. The presented technique is based on principal component perturbations and can be used for data augmentation to train object detection models. The numerical experiments performed with the YOLO model showed that the proposed method improved AP50 on the test set for transport aircraft detection, with statistical significance confirmed by bootstrap analysis.

nodes.name: Conditional Multi-Step Prediction for Distributed Photovoltaic Clusters Using Implicit Neural Motion Field with Wind-Modulated Fourier Layer Under Limited Local Meteorological Sensing
nodes.venue: Symmetry
nodes.abstract: Regional meteorological information does not fully resolve local microclimatic variability, while moving clouds over varied terrain cause dynamic spatial heterogeneity in distributed photovoltaic (PV) power output. This study performs retrospective evaluation adopting observed future period meteorology as known inputs. This study proposes an implicit neural motion field (INMF) for multi-step conditional prediction of distributed PV power under limited local meteorological sensing. Learnable site coordinates, site embeddings, and radial basis function interpolation map discrete site states onto a regular latent grid. A neural ordinary differential equation evolves this field through a wind-modulated Fourier layer, in which wind speed conditions spectral amplitudes and wind direction conditions spectral phases. An auxiliary irradiance-consistency term regularizes the temporal relationship between predicted outputs and irradiance. The model is evaluated on 20 rooftop PV sites in Hong Kong using observed target-period meteorology. Joint wind modulation reduces RMSE by 8.9–18.5% across the four evaluated step horizons. In the ablation experiments, phase modulation and the irradiance-consistency term yield reductions in aggregated-series RMSE. The latent coordinates represent learned intersite relationships, and the evolving field provides a representation of PV dynamics under the specified meteorological conditions.

nodes.name: CenterScan-Mamba: an efficient state space model for intelligent hyperspectral image classification
nodes.venue: International Conference on Communication, Sensing, and Intelligent Computing (CSIC 2026)
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification—assigning a land-cover label to every pixel from hundreds of contiguous spectral bands—is a core intelligent-computing task in remote sensing, today driven by convolutional and, more recently, transformer backbones. State space models (SSMs) such as Mamba are an appealing third option: they read a sequence in linear time. Yet a plain raster scan treats an image patch as if it were causal text. The central pixel we actually want to label then ends up buried in the middle of the sequence. We revisit that choice. We propose CenterScan-Mamba, a compact spectral–spatial SSM built on two ideas. A center-prioritized scan reorders the patch tokens so the target pixel is read last, letting its hidden state absorb the whole neighborhood. A center-anchored global readout then fuses pooled context with the central token. A gated spectral branch over the pixel’s own spectral curve is added on top. On three standard benchmarks the model is competitive with strong CNN and transformer baselines while remaining compact (∼195K parameters, sub-million). The scan order is not a cosmetic choice. On the hard Indian Pines scene it lifts accuracy by 3.16 points over a raster scan, and pulls a vanilla Mamba up from 79.26% to the mid-nineties. Ablations isolate each part, and the classification maps make the gap visible.

nodes.name: Application Value of Multimodal Imaging Three-Dimensional Fusion in Surgery for Central Region Tumors: A Retrospective Controlled Study
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the clinical value of preoperative multimodal imaging three-dimensional (3D) fusion reconstruction in microsurgical treatment of tumors involving the central region, and to evaluate its impact on the extent of resection, intraoperative venous preservation, and postoperative complications. Methods A total of 50 patients with central region tumors who underwent microsurgical treatment in the Department of Neurosurgery, Hubei No. 3 People's Hospital of Jianghan University, from February 2021 to February 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Based on whether preoperative multimodal imaging 3D fusion was employed to assist surgical planning, patients were divided into the 3D fusion group (n = 25) and the conventional imaging group (n = 25). In the 3D fusion group, 3D reconstruction was performed based on multimodal imaging data to formulate individualized surgical approaches and venous protection strategies. In the conventional imaging group, surgical plans were determined solely by routine imaging interpretation. General baseline characteristics, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, extent of resection, critical superficial venous injury, postoperative complications, and Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score at discharge were compared between the two groups. Results No significant differences were observed between the two groups in sex, age, pathological type, lesion laterality, maximum tumor diameter, or preoperative peritumoral edema grade (all P > 0.05). The gross total resection (GTR) rate was significantly higher in the 3D fusion group than in the conventional imaging group [88.0% (22/25) vs. 64.0% (16/25), P < 0.05]. Operative time and intraoperative blood loss were significantly lower in the 3D fusion group [(182.6 ± 34.8) min vs. (214.3 ± 39.7) min; (226.0 ± 82.5) mL vs. (308.0 ± 96.4) mL; both P < 0.01]. The incidence of critical superficial venous injury was significantly lower in the 3D fusion group [8.0% (2/25) vs. 32.0% (8/25), P < 0.05]. The 3D fusion group demonstrated lower rates of postoperative cerebral edema exacerbation, new-onset or worsened neurological deficits, and overall complications compared with the conventional imaging group, while KPS at discharge was significantly higher (all P < 0.05). The agreement rates between preoperative 3D fusion reconstruction and intraoperative findings regarding superficial venous morphological configuration, predominant venous course, and tumor–vein spatial relationship were 96.0%, 92.0%, and 100.0%, with Kappa values of 0.948, 0.881, and 1.000, respectively. Conclusion Multimodal imaging 3D fusion reconstruction can accurately delineate the spatial relationships between central region tumors and the superficial venous system, thereby facilitating optimization of surgical strategies, improving the extent of resection, and reducing critical venous injury and postoperative complications. This technique demonstrates substantial clinical application value in surgery for central region tumors.

nodes.name: A Spatial Model of Chronic Wasting Disease and the Optimal Placement of a Sight-Based Cull
nodes.abstract: Abstract Chronic wasting disease (CWD) is a fatal prion disease of cervids that spreads by direct contact and through a persistent environmental reservoir. We ask where and when a cull restricted to the clinically affected animals that field crews can identify should be placed on a real landscape, and what it can achieve. We formulate a five-compartment (susceptible, exposed, pre-clinical, clinical, environmental) reaction–diffusion model on a surface built from digital elevation data, with land cover setting the carrying capacity and slope and land cover setting an anisotropic diffusion tensor. We optimize a space- and time-dependent removal rate on the clinical class, computing gradients with the exact discrete adjoint of the finite element scheme. A closed-form bound gives the lowest control reproduction number such a cull can reach. With our parameters, pre-clinical animals generate 39.5% of local transmission, and maximal effort leaves it at or above 1.36 across our sweep. Simulations across reservoir persistence and transmissibility confirm that the optimal cull slows but never halts the invasion. The front retains 56–94% of its uncontrolled speed, and the control recovers 7–53% of the accumulated loss of susceptible deer. Where the herd is depleted, optimal effort forms a ring at the leading edge, 12–19 km ahead of the clinical peak. Cumulative incidence can rise under control even as per-capita risk falls, because the cull keeps more susceptible deer alive. On three Colorado landscapes, terrain and land cover barely change the benefit, and the cull needs 26–35% less effort, since less ground carries the invasion. nodes.name: A Multi-Criteria Geostatistical Framework Integrating Centrality Measures and Satellite Validation for PM2.5 Monitoring Network Expansion in Upper Northern Thailand
nodes.venue: Mathematics
nodes.abstract: Upper Northern Thailand is a critical region reflecting the severity of seasonal PM2.5 pollution and its transboundary spread, yet accurate spatial monitoring remains difficult due to complex mountainous terrain and a sparse network of physical monitoring stations. To resolve this observational limitation under a fixed sensor budget, this study develops a multi-criteria spatial optimization framework using weighted-sum scalarization to identify optimal locations for network expansion. We integrate set-dependent geostatistical Average Kriging Variance (AKV) reduction, meteorological correlation graphs, and cross-source satellite discrepancy into a unified combinatorial objective. Feature selection reveals that coupling rainfall, relative humidity, and temperature yields the best predictive performance, achieving an R2 of 0.8785 and minimizing RMSE to 33.91μg/m3 under Universal Kriging (UK). While Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Universal Kriging produce consistent spatial patterns, UK systematically secures superior variance reduction by accounting for coordinate-based spatial trends. Comparing optimization algorithms demonstrates distinct search dynamics: Genetic Algorithms (GAs) converge faster for smaller network expansion sizes, whereas Simulated Annealing (SA) becomes more scalable and efficient when adding 20 or more stations. Incorporating graph centrality measures (betweenness centrality and clustering coefficient) actively promotes spatial dispersion and prevents candidate stations from clustering redundantly in high-uncertainty areas. Furthermore, retrospective ground-station masking experiments demonstrate that the framework reliably targets genuine observational blind spots, reducing out-of-sample prediction RMSE by up to 40.98% upon network expansion. The proposed framework provides a practical, data-driven decision-support screening tool for environmental agencies seeking cost-effective air quality infrastructure expansion in data-sparse regions.

nodes.name: A Method for 3D Morphological Measurement and Cutting Point Localization of Green Asparagus Based on Improved YOLOv8n-seg and RGB-D Data
nodes.abstract: Abstract To address the difficulties in recognition and localization caused by the curved and irregular growth forms of green asparagus in natural environments, with parts of the rootstalk hidden in soil, and the challenge of balancing detection accuracy and speed with traditional instance segmentation algorithms during automated harvesting operations, a lightweight green asparagus instance segmentation model named SES-YOLO based on improved YOLOv8n-seg is proposed. First, the StarNet lightweight backbone network is used to replace the original backbone structure, reducing the computational burden of the model. Second, the C2fDWConv_Strip module is designed by integrating depthwise separable convolution and strip convolution to enhance the feature extraction capability for slender targets. Then, the EGAP module is embedded into the SPPF layer to improve edge detail perception and anti-interference capability, and the MPDIoU loss function is adopted to optimize bounding box regression accuracy. Finally, a method combining image masks with depth information to calculate the length and diameter of green asparagus and locate the cutting point is employed. Experimental results show that SES-YOLO achieves precision, recall, and mAP@50 of 98.6%, 97.3%, and 99.3%, respectively. Compared to the baseline model, the parameter count is reduced by 38.1%, and the computational load is decreased by 22.3%. The average relative measurement errors for asparagus length and diameter are 1.97% and 2.07%, respectively, and the average cutting point localization error is 0.34 cm. The model's inference speed on the Jetson Orin NX edge device is 38.69 FPS, which is 58.4% higher than the baseline model. This model maintains high accuracy while possessing good lightweight and real-time performance, making it suitable for embedded deployment scenarios such as green asparagus harvesting robots, providing reliable technical support for achieving automated selective harvesting.
